The mdn and sieve entry points refer back to the same section. description:
src/lib.rs:129, 275, 321 declare three handler-registration entry points (`register_mail_handlers`, `register_mdn_handlers`, `register_sieve_handlers`). The doc on each describes what method names get registered but does NOT mention what happens when those names conflict with pre-existing entries in the dispatcher.

Crate dependency `jmap_server::Dispatcher::register` (crate-jmap-server/src/lib.rs:~280) is implemented as:

```
pub fn register(&mut self, method: impl Into<String>, handler: Arc<dyn JmapHandler<CallerCtx>>) {
    self.handlers.insert(method.into(), handler);
}
```

Silent overwrite. No error returned. No log.

Consumers will hit this in three realistic scenarios:

1. **Double-registration.** A caller who calls `register_mail_handlers` twice (e.g. once during initialization, once when refreshing a backend) silently loses the first set's handlers. No diagnostic.

2. **Custom override.** A caller wants to override one or two RFC 8621 method handlers with their own implementation. The natural pattern is to call `register_mail_handlers` first (to set up the 26 defaults), then `dispatcher.register("Email/get", my_override)` to replace one. This works — but the inverse (register the override first, then call `register_mail_handlers`) silently undoes the override. Order-dependent behavior is undocumented.

3. **Extension cross-collision.** If a future extension's `register_*` function uses a name that overlaps with another (vendor-prefixed methods like `MyVendor/foo`), order matters and silent overwrite hides the conflict.

Contract issue: the registration functions advertise an "additive" mental model but the underlying primitive is "replacing". Either:
- Document the overwrite-wins semantics explicitly in the doc comment.
- OR have `Dispatcher::register` return `Option<Arc<dyn JmapHandler<...>>>` (the previously-registered handler, if any) so callers can detect collisions.

Defensive shape would be to have `register_mail_handlers` return `Vec<(&'static str, Option<Arc<dyn JmapHandler<...>>>)>` — list of `(method_name, prior_handler)` for diagnostics. But that affects every sibling extension-server's identical entry-point shape.

Priority P2 because the failure mode is observable in CI (the second registration wins, tests would catch it) but the contract is currently invisible in docs.

Cookie-cutter amplification: all 7 sibling extension-server crates have the same shape; documenting here without propagation will create drift between mail-server's doc and the siblings'.
title: register_*_handlers doc does not specify silent-overwrite semantics
